claims.claim: Spring was cold for about 20 days, then warm at the end of April. Early summer was cool and rainy, and the year ended warmer than usual.
claims.note: Both describe a cold spring and wet early summer.

claims.claim: The Consorzio reportedly judged the season unstable overall, with adequate water and temperatures slightly above average.
claims.note: Via a producer sheet seen in a search summary.

claims.claim: Constant rain flooded some vineyards, and summer brought significant thunderstorms. One producer recorded a heavy September storm.
Frost, hail and flowering were not described in any source read.
Harvest started only three or four days earlier than normal. By 4 October one producer had nearly finished picking for Amarone and Valpolicella, with healthy grapes and high sugar.
The harvest was the largest of the decade.
No drying conditions for autumn 2018 and winter 2019 were found.
Wines have lower anthocyanin and tannin, a less structured profile, pronounced acidity and complex fruit. Less body than 2016 or 2017.
claims.note: Two sources agree. Producers and merchants are more positive.

claims.claim: Italy's Finest Wines gives three stars and calls results not always consistent. Producer sources call it a high-quality vintage.

conflicts: Quality: independent charts say lighter and less consistent. Producers and merchants say high quality with ageing potential.
Vogadori says the vintage resembles 2016 with heavier clusters. Wine Scholar Guild says less body than 2016.
gaps: No Consorzio Tutela Vini Valpolicella vintage rating or official harvest report was found or read.
Drying conditions and an independent yield figure not found.

sheet.vintage: 2018 was a wet, cool-then-warm year with a big crop. The Amarone is a little lighter, with bright acidity.
